title: AssetCore Walkthrough
headline: Every workflow, in the order a working day runs
tagline: A guided pass through the whole of AssetCore on production — what each part is for, what to type, and what you should see.
intro: Each card opens with what the feature is, in words you can say out loud, then the exact data to enter. Everything you create is prefixed UAT so it can be found and archived afterwards — this is production, and NGML's two evaluators (Paul O. and Hayatu S.) work in the same organisation. Read card 02 before you sign in as anyone else: the site allows only ten sign-ins every fifteen minutes, for everyone at once.
url_hint: The app is live at https://myassetcore.com. Nothing needs starting.

sections.title: Before you start
sections.blurb: AssetCore is an asset-management and maintenance system for gas infrastructure: it keeps the register of every physical asset, schedules the maintenance and inspections that keep them safe, turns what inspectors find into jobs, and tracks the money, compliance and risk around all of it. These two cards get you signed in and set up so the rest of the session runs without a lockout.

tests.title: Sign in to production and read the dashboard
tests.intro: What it is: the Operations Dashboard is the first thing everyone lands on — a live summary of the whole network. Network Health is the average condition score across assets; the tiles count assets, open work, overdue preventive maintenance and compliance alerts; Active Alerts lists what needs attention now. The left-hand menu is filtered by role, so what you see as System Admin is the fullest view anyone gets.
steps: Open https://myassetcore.com.
Sign in with your own System Admin login.
Read each tile aloud and say what it counts. Open the All my locations filter at the top and note it narrows every page to one region.
Walk down the left-hand menu once, top to bottom, naming each section — the cards below visit every one.
tests.expect: The dashboard loads for the Demo Client organisation with a Network Health score, the six tiles and an Active Alerts list. Your name and System Admin sit at the bottom of the menu.

tests.title: Agree how you will switch between people
tests.intro: Why this card exists: the sign-in form allows ten sign-ins per fifteen minutes from one internet address, and counts successful ones too. Until the evening before this session that limit was shared by every user on the site — a bug found while writing this plan, now fixed — but you and your colleague sitting in the same office still share one address between you. Plan the session so you rarely sign out.
steps: Keep this browser window signed in as yourself (the owner) all session.
Open a second browser (or a private window) for the office roles — HSE Officer, Operations Manager, and later the Viewer, Auditor and Engineer.
Ask your colleague to play the Field Technician on their own laptop. The job-execution cards then run as a real hand-off between two people.
Keep a running tally of sign-ins on paper. Never make more than eight inside fifteen minutes.
If a sign-in ever says Too many attempts. Wait about 15 minutes and try again., stop signing in and carry on with an owner-window card instead.
tests.expect: You have three places to be three people at once, and a tally sheet. The whole plan needs about twelve sign-ins spread across the session — well inside the limit if they are paced.

sections.title: Set up the organisation
sections.blurb: Before any asset can exist, the organisation needs its geography and its vocabulary: locations (a region or state), sites inside them (a physical facility), categories (what kind of asset something is), the people who will use it, and the rule for who signs off spending. All of this lives under Admin.

tests.title: Create a location and a site
tests.intro: What it is: the location hierarchy. A location is a region — Lagos, Delta — and a site is a real facility inside it, like a metering yard or compressor station. Every asset sits on a site, and a user can be limited to certain locations or sites, which is how a regional engineer only sees their own patch.
steps: Admin → Locations → + Add Location.
Location Name UAT Lagos · Short Code UATLG. Save.
Admin → Sites → add a site.
Site Name UAT Apapa Metering Yard · Site Code UAT-APP01 · Region South West · Location UAT Lagos. Save.
tests.expect: UAT Lagos appears as a location card reading 1 site, and UAT Apapa Metering Yard lists under it. Leaving the site name or code empty is refused with Name and code are required.

tests.title: Create an asset category
tests.intro: What it is: a category is the kind of asset — Metering Station, Compressor, Pressure Regulator. It is required on every asset, it is how the register is filtered, and it can carry default depreciation settings for everything in it. A brand-new organisation has none, so this has to exist before the first asset.
steps: Admin → Asset Categories → add one.
Category Name UAT Metering Station · Short Code UATMS. Save.
tests.expect: UAT Metering Station appears in the category list and will be offered as an Asset type on the asset form.

tests.title: Read the organisation's rules — look, don't change
tests.intro: What it is: Configuration holds two organisation-wide settings. Health thresholds: when an asset's condition score drops below 50% the system raises an inspection for it automatically, and below 30% it drafts a work order. Depreciation defaults: the method (straight-line, declining balance or none), whether it runs from the install or purchase date, and the default useful life and residual value. Only the System Admin and Operations Manager can change these.
steps: Admin → Configuration.
Read the health thresholds and the depreciation defaults aloud.
Settings → Organisation → look at the Currency block: every figure is held in the base currency, and a second currency can be shown beside it at a rate someone types in.
Change nothing here. Both screens are organisation-wide on production and NGML's evaluators would see the change.
tests.expect: Configuration shows the two thresholds and the depreciation defaults with the note Only a System Admin or Operations Manager can change this. Currency shows NGN as the base with no second currency.

tests.title: Invite the team — one account per role
tests.intro: What it is: AssetCore has seven roles, and each sees a different app. System Admin — everything. Operations Manager — runs operations and sites, approves spend, cannot manage people. Maintenance Engineer — works and updates jobs, can approve. Field Technician — does the jobs assigned to them. HSE / Compliance Officer — inspections, defects, licences, audits and risk. Auditor — reads everything plus the audit log. Executive / Viewer — reads, never writes.
steps: Use six addresses you can receive mail at. Most inboxes accept a +tag — yourname+uat-ops@yourdomain delivers to yourname@yourdomain.
Admin → Users & Roles → + Invite User. Full name UAT Ops Manager, email your +uat-ops address, role Operations Manager. Leave Access scope and Extra permissions untouched. Send Invite.
Repeat for UAT Maintenance Engineer (+uat-eng), UAT Field Technician (+uat-tech), UAT HSE Officer (+uat-hse), UAT Auditor (+uat-audit) and UAT Viewer (+uat-view), each with its matching role.

Each invite either shows a set-password link on screen or emails one. Open each link in the second browser, set the password to UatWalk2026!, and do not sign in yet — setting a password costs no sign-in; signing in does.
While the invite form is open once more, try pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> in the name field instead of clicking Send — see card 37.
tests.expect: Six invites go out, each with its own link. Users & Roles then lists seven members — you plus six — each Active with the right role label. Setting a password returns you to the sign-in page rather than signing you in.

tests.title: Decide who signs off job spend — the approval matrix
tests.intro: What it is: the approval matrix says which role must sign off what, by amount. A band of ₦1,000 to ₦500,000 on work-order spend → Operations Manager means any job costing inside that range needs an Operations Manager's approval before it is authorised. The system also refuses anyone approving their own request, and anyone deciding a request that is waiting on a different role.
steps: Approvals → Matrix → add a band.
Name UAT job spend up to ₦500,000 · Applies to Work order · Kind Spend authorisation · Floor 1000 · Ceiling 500000 · Signed off by Operations Manager. Save.
Now try to save a second band with Floor 90000 and Ceiling 5000.
tests.expect: The first band appears in the matrix with its range and Operations Manager. The second is refused in place with The ceiling has to be above the floor. — a sentence, not an error code.

sections.title: The asset register
sections.blurb: The asset register is the heart of the product: one record per physical asset, with its identity (the AIN — asset identification number), where it is, what it is worth, when it was last and next maintained, and a live health score built from inspections, defects, overdue work and risk. Assets can be entered by hand, imported from a spreadsheet, labelled with QR codes and found in the field by scanning.

tests.title: Register an asset by hand
tests.intro: What it is: the full asset record. The starred fields are required; the rest feed other parts of the product — value and useful life drive depreciation, the maintenance dates drive the calendar, and the coordinates put the asset on the map.
steps: Assets → + Add Asset.
Asset name UAT Apapa Custody Meter Skid A · AIN UAT-MTR-0001 · Asset type UAT Metering Station · Location UAT Lagos · Site UAT Apapa Metering Yard · Status Operational.
Manufacturer Emerson · Model Daniel 3818 Ultrasonic · Serial UAT-SN-24001 · Install date 15/03/2022 · Purchase date 20/02/2022 · Runtime 18240.
Asset value (₦) 185000000 · Last maintenance 01/07/2026 · Next maintenance 01/10/2026.
Depreciation method Organisation default · Useful life 15 · Salvage value (₦) 18500000 · Tags custody-transfer, critical · Latitude 6.4474 · Longitude 3.3645.
Save. Then try saving a second asset with the AIN left empty.
tests.expect: The asset saves and appears in the register as UAT-MTR-0001, Operational, with a health bar and next maintenance 1 Oct 26. The empty-AIN attempt is refused and names what is missing.

tests.title: Read the asset record and its health working
tests.intro: What it is: the health score is AssetCore's single most important number, and it explains itself. Show the working lists the five signals — inspection condition, open defects, overdue maintenance, risk level, and age against useful life — each with its score and weight. A signal with no evidence yet is left out rather than counted as zero, and the page says so. This card is the before picture for the inspection in card 16.
steps: Assets → View on UAT-MTR-0001.
Read the Financials block: purchase value, book value (NBV — what it is worth after depreciation) and accumulated depreciation.
Press Show the working. Note the headline score and which signals say no data.
Write down the score. You will come back to it.
tests.expect: The panel shows ₦185,000,000.00 as purchase value and a book value below it. Show the working lists all five signals with weights; the ones with no evidence yet (no inspection, for instance) are marked no data with a reason, and the header says how many of the five were used.

tests.title: Import two assets from a spreadsheet
tests.intro: What it is: bulk import, for loading an existing register in one go. Category, location and site are matched by name or short code (capital letters don't matter), dates are written YYYY-MM-DD, maintenance dates are required on every row, and a bad row is reported rather than silently dropped.
steps: Assets → Import CSV and download the template it offers, to see the columns.

In any text editor, save a file uat-assets.csv containing exactly these three lines:
ain,name,category,location,site,status,manufacturer,model,serial_number,install_date,purchase_date,runtime_hours,value,last_maintenance_date,next_maintenance_date,tags,lat,lng
UAT-PRG-0001,UAT Apapa Pressure Regulator 1,UAT Metering Station,UAT Lagos,UAT Apapa Metering Yard,operational,Fisher,EZH-1,UAT-SN-24002,2023-05-10,2023-04-02,9800,42000000,2026-08-01,2026-11-01,regulator,6.4480,3.3651
UAT-VLV-0001,UAT Apapa Inlet Isolation Valve,UAT Metering Station,UAT Lagos,UAT Apapa Metering Yard,operational,Cameron,T31,UAT-SN-24003,2021-11-20,2021-10-15,31000,12500000,2026-06-15,2026-12-15,valve,6.4468,3.3639
Import it.
Search the register for UAT.
tests.expect: The import reports both rows as created. Searching UAT shows three assets — Skid A, the regulator and the valve — all on UAT Apapa Metering Yard.

tests.title: Print QR labels and use the scan page
tests.intro: What it is: every asset can carry a QR label. A technician standing at a piece of equipment scans it and lands straight on its record — history, open jobs and condition — without searching. Labels prints whatever the register is currently filtered to, four to a row.
steps: On Assets, search UAT so only the three UAT assets show, then press Labels.
Check each label names its AIN, then print or print-preview the sheet (allow pop-ups if the browser asks).
Open https://myassetcore.com/scan. On a phone, point the camera at one label; on a laptop, type UAT-MTR-0001 into the tag field.
tests.expect: The sheet shows three labels, each with a QR code and its AIN. The scan page resolves UAT-MTR-0001 to Skid A's card, showing Manufacturer Emerson and its installation date.

tests.title: Attach a photo and open it full size
tests.intro: What it is: photos and documents on the asset record — nameplates, datasheets, before-and-after pictures. Files are only ever served to a signed-in user whose access covers that asset.
steps: Have any photo of equipment ready on your computer.
Assets → Edit on UAT-MTR-0001 → Images → choose the photo. Save.
Open the asset and click the thumbnail. Close the full-size view with <kbd>Escape</kbd>.
tests.expect: The photo uploads, shows as a thumbnail on the record, opens full size in a lightbox, and closes on Escape. (This has never been tested before — it needs a real file picker.)

sections.title: Stores and planned maintenance
sections.blurb: Spare Parts is the parts store: what is on the shelf, what it cost, and every movement in or out, so stock can be reserved against a job and drawn when the job closes. Maintenance holds the preventive schedules — the recurring work that stops things breaking — which generate tasks on their own at the frequency you set.

tests.title: Add a spare part and record stock going out
tests.intro: What it is: each part carries a reorder level. When stock falls to it or below, the part is flagged Reorder. Every change is recorded as a movement — a receipt, an issue, a return or an adjustment — so the balance always has a reason behind it.
steps: Spare Parts → Add Part.

Part number UAT-SP-0001 · Category Instrumentation · Name UAT Ultrasonic transducer pair · Unit each · Unit cost (₦) 420000 · Reorder level 3 · Reorder quantity 4 · Supplier Emerson Nigeria · Storage location Apapa Store / Bin 4 · Opening stock 6. Add part.
On its row press Adjust → Issue · Quantity 3 · Reference UAT issued to Apapa calibration crew. Watch the preview line before recording.
Record movement.
tests.expect: The part saves with 6 each on hand. The adjust dialog previews Stock moves to 3 each. After recording, on-hand reads 3, the row gains an amber Reorder badge, and At or below reorder level goes up by one.

tests.title: Create a preventive maintenance schedule
tests.intro: What it is: a PM schedule is recurring planned work — quarterly calibration, monthly lubrication. The system generates a task each time one falls due, puts it on the calendar and chases it if it goes overdue. Attaching it to an asset is what makes those tasks appear on the asset's own record and count towards its condition score. (This form had no Asset field at all until the evening before this session — found while writing this plan, and fixed.)
steps: Maintenance → + Schedule PM.
Title UAT Quarterly meter calibration — Skid A · Description Verify against master meter; check transducer paths · Frequency Quarterly · First due 19/09/2026.
Asset UAT-MTR-0001 — UAT Apapa Custody Meter Skid A · Default assignee UAT Maintenance Engineer. Save Schedule.
Read the line under the Asset field aloud — it says what happens to a schedule left without one.
tests.expect: The schedule lists as Quarterly against UAT Apapa Custody Meter Skid A, with its first task due 19 Sept 26 and the Maintenance Engineer as default assignee. Leaving the asset blank is still allowed — some schedules are site-wide — and the note says what that costs.

sections.title: The core loop: inspection → defect → job
sections.blurb: This is the chain the product exists for. An inspection checks an asset and rates its condition 1–5; what it finds goes on the defect register; a defect becomes a work order (a job); the job is assigned, worked, costed, signed off and closed; closing it resolves the defect and moves the asset's health. Four roles take part — run it as the hand-off it really is, with your colleague as the technician.

tests.title: Schedule an inspection against the asset
tests.intro: What it is: inspections are the eyes on the network — routine condition checks, safety inspections, regulatory integrity checks. Attaching one to an asset is what lets its rating reach that asset's health score. (Checklist templates exist in the system but there is no screen to create one yet, so this inspection records free-text findings.)
steps: In the second browser, sign in as the HSE Officer. (Sign-in 2.)
Inspections → + New Inspection.

Title UAT Condition inspection — Custody Meter Skid A · Type Condition · Scheduled date 12/09/2026 · Checklist — No checklist — · Asset UAT-MTR-0001 (the Site fills itself in) · Inspector UAT HSE Officer. Create.
tests.expect: The inspection lists as Scheduled with ASSET UAT-MTR-0001 and SITE UAT Apapa Metering Yard. Choosing the asset set the site automatically.

tests.title: Complete it with a poor rating, and watch the asset's health take it in
tests.intro: What it is: completion is where the inspection counts. The 1–5 condition rating is required — the system will not complete an inspection without one, because a health score built on a rating nobody gave would be a guess. The rating becomes a quarter of the asset's health score.
steps: As the HSE Officer, press Complete on the inspection.
Try Mark Complete with no rating chosen, and note the button stays disabled.
Choose 2 — Poor. Findings Path 3 transducer signal-to-noise below 20 dB; flow computer display intermittently blank; light corrosion on inlet flange bolts. Mark Complete.
Back in your owner window, open UAT-MTR-0001 → Show the working, and compare with the score from card 09.
tests.expect: Completion is impossible without a rating. Afterwards the inspection moves to Completed, and Skid A's breakdown now carries Inspection condition 25/100 — Rated 2 of 5 on 12 Sept 2026. The headline still reconciles with the signals listed beneath it.

tests.title: Log the defect the inspection found
tests.intro: What it is: the defect register is the list of things actually wrong, each with a severity. Linking a defect to the inspection that found it is what lets anyone trace a job back to the walk-round that started it. Severity sets the priority of any job raised from it.
steps: As the HSE Officer, Defects → new defect.

What is wrong UAT Path 3 transducer signal degraded · Detail SNR 17 dB against a 20 dB minimum; custody measurement uncertainty exceeds tolerance. · Severity Major · Asset UAT-MTR-0001 · Site UAT Apapa Metering Yard · Found during UAT Condition inspection — Custody Meter Skid A · Identified on 12/09/2026 · Fix by 26/09/2026 · Category instrumentation. Save.
tests.expect: A defect with a DEF-2026-… reference appears on the register as Major · Open, naming the asset and showing where it came from: the inspection it was found during.

tests.title: Turn the defect into a work order and assign it
tests.intro: What it is: a work order is a job. Raising one from a defect carries the link both ways — the job says what it came from, the defect shows its job — and closing the job resolves the defect. The priority comes from the severity: a Major defect makes a High-priority job.
steps: In the second browser, sign out and sign in as the Operations Manager. (Sign-in 3.)
Defects → open UAT Path 3 transducer signal degraded → Raise a work order. SLA due 19/09/2026. Raise it.
Open the new job from Work Orders → Edit → Estimated cost (₦) 420000 · Assign to UAT Field Technician. Save.
tests.expect: A WO-2026-… job exists at High priority, type Corrective, showing Raised from DEF-2026-… · Closing this job resolves it. The defect now shows its job. After saving, the job is assigned to the Field Technician and records who assigned it and when.

tests.title: The technician picks it up: checklist, parts, spend request
tests.intro: What it is: the technician's side. Assigned work arrives in My Open Work and as a notification — nobody should have to type a URL to find their job. On the job they build a checklist of steps, reserve parts from the store, and send the cost for approval.
steps: On your colleague's laptop, open https://myassetcore.com and sign in as the Field Technician. (Sign-in 4.)
Check the dashboard's My Open Work tile and the notification bell — open the job from there.
Checklist: add Isolate meter run and depressurise, Replace path 3 transducer pair, Re-zero and verify against master meter. Tick the first.
Parts: choose UAT-SP-0001 — UAT Ultrasonic transducer pair, quantity 1, Add.
Spend authorisation: Request spend approval, note Replacement transducer pair for path 3, Send for approval.
Move the job to In Progress.
tests.expect: The job is in the technician's own list and notification. The checklist reads 1/3 done. The parts line reads 1× UAT Ultrasonic transducer pair · Reserved with a ₦420,000 total. The spend section reads With Operations Manager · ₦420,000 · Pending.

tests.title: Approve the spend as the Operations Manager
tests.intro: What it is: the sign-off. The request went to the Operations Manager because the ₦420,000 cost falls inside the band set in card 07. Someone holding approval rights, but in a different role, cannot decide it — and nobody can approve their own request. Worth saying aloud: an approval records the sign-off; it does not yet physically stop a job from being closed.
steps: In the second browser (still the Operations Manager), open Approvals → Waiting on me.
Open the request, add the note Approved — critical custody meter, and Approve.
tests.expect: The request is listed under Waiting on me and names the technician as requester. After approving, it moves to Approved and the technician's job shows the decision.

tests.title: Finish and close the job
tests.intro: What it is: the job's lifecycle. Each move is limited to what makes sense next (a closed job cannot reopen), every change is stamped with who and when, and closing does real work: it draws reserved parts out of the store and resolves the defect the job came from.
steps: On your colleague's laptop, tick the other two checklist steps (3/3).
Move the job In Progress → Inspection → Closed, reading the Move to buttons offered at each step.
tests.expect: Each step offers only valid next statuses. Once Closed, the Move to section disappears — there is no way back. The part line reads Taken.

tests.title: Check the loop closed everywhere
tests.intro: What it is: the payoff — one job moved several parts of the system. This card checks each one from the owner's chair.
steps: Defects: the UAT defect now reads Resolved.
Spare Parts: UAT-SP-0001 on hand fell from 3 to 2, and its history shows a movement Used on job · WO-2026-….
Analytics → Performance: MTTR (mean time to repair) now reports a figure, including the job you just closed.
Assets → UAT-MTR-0001 → Show the working: open defects no longer counts the resolved one.
tests.expect: Defect Resolved; part stock 2 with a consumption movement naming the job; MTTR shows hours per repair and a job count; and the asset's open-defects signal has recovered.

sections.title: Money: depreciation
sections.blurb: Depreciation writes an asset's value down over its useful life, so the register shows what equipment is actually worth today — its net book value (NBV). AssetCore keeps it as a proper schedule of yearly charges that are posted, like entries in a ledger, so the book value always has an audit trail.

tests.title: Build a depreciation schedule for the asset
tests.intro: What it is: the preview shows the full year-by-year schedule before anything is saved, worked out from the asset's own record. Straight-line spreads the value evenly: (cost − salvage value) ÷ useful life, per year.
steps: Depreciation → New Schedule (or Create first schedule).
Asset UAT-MTR-0001 · Method Straight line. Leave the basis override closed — it reads the asset's own figures.
Read the preview: method, cost, salvage, life and start date, then the table.
Create schedule. Do not post periods — posting writes entries to the books; on production, leave that decision for real data.
tests.expect: The basis reads cost ₦185,000,000, salvage ₦18,500,000, life 15 years, from the install date 2022-03-15. Every yearly charge is ₦11,100,000.00 — that is (185,000,000 − 18,500,000) ÷ 15. After creating, the register lists the schedule with 0 / 15 posted.

sections.title: Compliance and risk
sections.blurb: Compliance tracks the licences and certificates an operator must hold — each with an issuing authority and an expiry date, flagged well before it lapses — and the audits carried out against standards like ISO 9001. The risk register scores what could go wrong on a 5×5 grid of likelihood against consequence, twice: before controls (inherent) and after them (residual).

tests.title: Record a licence that is about to expire
tests.intro: What it is: the licence register is how an operator avoids running a facility on a lapsed permit. Anything inside its expiry window is flagged Expiring, and counted on the dashboard's Compliance Alerts tile.
steps: In the second browser, sign out and sign in as the HSE Officer. (Sign-in 5.)
Compliance → Licences & Certificates → + Add Licence.
Name UAT Custody Transfer Metering Licence — Apapa · Reference NMDPRA/CTM/2025/UAT-001 · Regulatory authority NMDPRA · Site UAT Apapa Metering Yard · Issued 01/10/2025 · Expiry 30/09/2026. Save.
tests.expect: The licence lists as Expiring with 18d left (30 Sept is 18 days after the 12th). The Expiring filter count goes up by one, and so does the dashboard's Compliance Alerts expiring figure.

tests.title: Run an audit from scheduled to completed, with a finding
tests.intro: What it is: audits record inspections against a standard, with a lifecycle — scheduled, in progress, completed — and an outcome that is required before completion. Each finding can be pushed straight onto the defect register, so an audit gap becomes tracked work.
steps: Compliance → Audits & Attestations → + New Audit.

Title UAT ISO 9001 surveillance audit — Apapa · Standard ISO 9001:2015 · ISO certificate reference UAT-9001-2026-01 · Audit date 12/09/2026 · Site UAT Apapa Metering Yard · Asset UAT-MTR-0001 · Stage Scheduled. Save.
Edit it to In progress, save; then to Completed with no outcome, and note the refusal. Choose outcome Pass with findings and save.
Open Findings: severity Major · clause ISO 9001 §7.1.5 · text Master meter calibration certificate expired in August; measurements since are not traceable. Save, then Raise a defect on it.
tests.expect: The form opens at Scheduled and saves first time. Completing without an outcome is refused with An outcome is required to complete an audit. The finding raises a DEF-2026-… and its button is replaced by On the register as DEF-2026-…, so it cannot be raised twice.

tests.title: Put a risk on the matrix, before and after controls
tests.intro: What it is: each risk is scored likelihood × consequence, 1–25, and banded Low, Medium, High or Extreme. Inherent is the risk with nothing in place; residual is what is left once the controls work. The gap between them shows what the controls are worth, and the residual feeds the asset's health score.
steps: Risk → new risk.
What could happen UAT Gas release at Skid A inlet flange during transducer change · Category Safety · Asset UAT-MTR-0001 · Site UAT Apapa Metering Yard.
Inherent: likelihood 4, consequence 5.
Controls in place Permit to work; isolation and depressurisation; portable gas detection; standby fire watch. Residual: likelihood 2, consequence 3. Review by 12/12/2026. Save.
Switch the matrix between Before controls and After controls.
tests.expect: The form reads Inherent 20 · Extreme and Residual 6 · Medium. The risk sits in the score-20 cell under the inherent view and moves to the score-6 cell under the residual view.

sections.title: Oversight: seeing the whole picture
sections.blurb: The rest of the product is how managers watch the network without opening records one at a time: reliability figures and a map, a calendar of everything scheduled, exportable reports, automatic chasing of anything left too long, connections to field devices and other systems, and a tamper-proof log of who did what.

tests.title: Analytics: reliability figures and the asset map
tests.intro: What it is: the maintenance KPIs. MTBF (mean time between failures) is how long assets run between breakdowns; MTTR (mean time to repair) is how long a repair takes once started; Availability is uptime as a percentage; the backlog sorts open work by age. Every figure shows its sample size, so a number built on one job never passes for a trend.
steps: Analytics → Performance. Read each tile and its explanatory line.
Switch the period between Last 30 days, Last 90 days and Last 12 months.
Open the Map tab.
tests.expect: Each tile has a unit and a sentence saying what it was built from. Changing the period changes MTBF and its operating-hours basis. The map plots the three UAT assets near Apapa and says how many assets are not shown for lack of coordinates; clicking a pin opens that asset.

tests.title: The calendar
tests.intro: What it is: one grid for every date in the system — work orders by due date, PM tasks, inspections — with overdue items in red and filters for each kind.
steps: Open Calendar on September 2026.
Find the UAT inspection on the 12th and the PM task on the 19th.
Untick Work orders, then move to October and back with Today.
tests.expect: The inspection sits on 12 Sept and the calibration task on 19 Sept. Unticking a type removes exactly those entries; month navigation works both ways.

tests.title: Generate a report and check it against the screen
tests.intro: What it is: exports for people outside the app — an asset register, a work-order summary, a compliance register, a PM history — as a spreadsheet or CSV. What leaves the building has to match what the screen says.
steps: Reports → Generate → Asset Register, format XLSX.
Download it from the Report Library and open it.
Find the UAT-MTR-0001 row and compare its health score and purchase value with the asset panel.
tests.expect: The report appears in the library naming you as requester, downloads as a real spreadsheet, and the Skid A row matches the screen: same health score, purchase value ₦185,000,000.

tests.title: Escalation rules: who gets chased, and when
tests.intro: What it is: escalations chase work left too long. A rule says if this kind of record has been in this state for this long, notify this role. Rules run every morning at 07:15 and on demand, and each record is escalated once, not every day. On production this rule applies to every record in the organisation, so this card creates it, explains it, and retires it.
steps: Admin → Escalations → + Add Rule.

Rule name UAT — critical work orders unassigned after 1 day · Applies to Work order · When it has been Unassigned · For at least 1 day · Only when priority is Critical · Notify Operations Manager. Save.
Change Applies to on a new rule to Compliance licence and note the trigger list shrinks to what makes sense for a licence. Cancel.
On the UAT rule press Retire and confirm.
tests.expect: The rule saves and lists with its condition and the role it notifies. The trigger options change with the record type. After Retire it stops being evaluated, and any escalations it already raised are kept.

tests.title: Devices and integrations — look, don't connect
tests.intro: What it is: Devices are field instruments and gateways that report live readings (over MQTT and similar protocols), each tied to an asset and site, and shown as Online, Offline, Error or Unprovisioned. Integrations connect AssetCore to other systems: SAP S/4HANA (sync the asset master, push work orders back), Termii SMS (text alerts to field technicians), and SCADA/Historian (process data — marked Coming soon).
steps: Open Devices and read the status summary and the supported protocols.
Optionally add one: name UAT Skid A flow transmitter gateway · IP 10.20.4.15 · Protocol MQTT · Serial UAT-GW-0001 · Firmware v2.3.1 · Asset UAT-MTR-0001 · Site UAT Apapa Metering Yard.
Open Integrations and read each card. Enter no credentials — secrets typed here are stored and used for real.
tests.expect: Devices shows the status chips and protocol list; a new device appears as Unprovisioned, because nothing has reported yet. Integrations shows SAP and Termii as configurable and SCADA as Coming soon.

tests.title: The audit log
tests.intro: What it is: an append-only record of every significant action — who, what, which record, when. Nobody can edit or delete an entry, the System Admin included. The Auditor role exists to read it.
steps: In the second browser, sign out and sign in as the Auditor. (Sign-in 6.)
Admin → Audit Log.
Find today's entries: the six invites, the work order closed, the defects raised.
Look for any control that edits or deletes an entry.
tests.expect: Admin shows only the Audit Log and a read-only Escalations tab — no Users & Roles, Locations or Configuration. Entries name the actor and time, and none can be changed.

sections.title: Who can do what
sections.blurb: Permissions are enforced by the server, not just by hiding buttons. For each role, check what it should see, then type a forbidden address straight into the browser — the page must refuse, not load. This is the most common way real systems leak data, which is why it gets its own section.

tests.title: Executive / Viewer: sees everything, changes nothing
tests.intro: What it is: the read-only role for leadership. It can open every operational page but create, edit or approve nothing, and it has no access to Admin or the audit log.
steps: Sign out, sign in as the Viewer. (Sign-in 7.)
Note Admin is missing from the menu, then type https://myassetcore.com/admin.
Open the UAT work order: look for Edit, status buttons, the comment box and Attach file.
Open Reports and look for a Generate control.
tests.expect: /admin sends you back to the dashboard. The work order shows no Edit, no Move-to buttons, no comment box and no Attach file. Reports offers the library and analytics but no way to generate.

tests.title: Field Technician: cannot reach management pages
tests.intro: What it is: the technician sees their work, the assets and the parts store — not finance, analytics or administration.
steps: On your colleague's laptop (still the Technician), type each of these: /reports, /analytics, /depreciation, /admin.
Open Risk and look for a way to add a risk.
tests.expect: All four addresses return to the dashboard. The technician can read the risk register but cannot create a risk.

tests.title: Maintenance Engineer: works jobs, cannot administer
tests.intro: What it is: engineers update assets and jobs and can approve, but cannot change the organisation, its people, the approval matrix or escalation rules.
steps: In the second browser, sign out and sign in as the Engineer. (Sign-in 8.)
Check the Maintenance page shows the calibration task assigned to you.
Type /admin. Open Approvals → Matrix. Open Settings → Organisation.
tests.expect: The PM task from card 14 is waiting for this user. /admin returns to the dashboard; the matrix cannot be edited; currency and organisation details are read-only.

tests.title: Operations Manager: runs sites and categories, not people
tests.intro: What it is: the one deliberate exception. The Operations Manager can maintain the location, site and category structure and the configuration, and can read the escalation rules and the audit log, but cannot invite or manage users, or change who approves what or who gets chased.
steps: Sign out, sign in as the Operations Manager. (Sign-in 9.)
Open Admin and list the tabs you get.
Look for Users & Roles; try adding an approval band; try adding an escalation rule.
tests.expect: Admin shows Locations, Sites, Asset Categories and Configuration, plus Escalations and the Audit Log to read — but not Users & Roles. No approval band or escalation rule can be added by this role.

sections.title: Things only a person can settle
sections.blurb: Three rounds of automated testing could not prove these, because the testing tool's simulated keyboard does not behave like a real one. With a physical keyboard and a phone they take five minutes, and they close the last open questions from earlier rounds.

tests.title: Keyboard: Enter submits, Tab moves, Escape closes
tests.intro: Why it matters: people who work fast, or cannot use a mouse, rely on the keyboard. Earlier rounds could not tell whether Enter submits a form or a real key press activates a button — this card settles it for good.
steps: On the sign-in page (when you next sign in), type the email and password and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> instead of clicking.
Admin → Users & Roles → Invite User: type a name and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> in the name field. Cancel if it submits.
Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> repeatedly on the dashboard and watch the focus ring move.
Open any modal and press <kbd>Escape</kbd>.
tests.expect: Enter submits both forms; Tab shows a visible focus ring moving in reading order; Escape closes the modal. If Enter does nothing, mark this Fail — that is a genuine accessibility defect nobody has been able to confirm until now.

tests.title: Phone width and dark mode
tests.intro: Why it matters: technicians work from phones, and the app has a dark theme for low light. Dark mode was reworked in round 3 for contrast and now remembers your choice.
steps: Open https://myassetcore.com on a phone and sign in as the Technician (or narrow a desktop window to phone width, to save a sign-in).
Open the dashboard, the work-order list, a work order, and the scan page. Open the menu.
Turn on dark mode from the account menu, reload, and read the dashboard and Analytics.
tests.expect: Nothing scrolls sideways; wide tables scroll inside their own box; the menu opens and closes; every button can be reached. Dark mode survives the reload and all text stays readable.

sections.title: Leave production tidy
sections.blurb: Everything this session made is prefixed UAT. Archiving hides records without deleting them, and every step can be undone.

tests.title: Archive what you made and disable the accounts
tests.intro: Why it matters: NGML's evaluators work in this organisation. Leaving UAT assets, alerts and accounts live muddies what they see. Archived assets drop out of the register, the dashboard and the map, but stay restorable.
steps: Assets: archive UAT-MTR-0001, UAT-PRG-0001 and UAT-VLV-0001 (confirm each).
Compliance: archive the UAT licence and the UAT audit.
Escalations: check the UAT rule shows as retired (card 30).
Admin → Users & Roles: Disable the six UAT members — or keep them if you will run this again.
Leave the UAT spare part, PM schedule, depreciation schedule, risk and defects: they are clearly labelled, and archiving the asset takes them out of the headline figures.
tests.expect: The three UAT assets vanish from the register, dashboard and map, and appear under Archived. The six members read Disabled, and a disabled account's next sign-in is refused with This account has been disabled. Ask an administrator to re-enable it.
